description: Coastal Resilience Evaluation and Siting Tool (CREST) is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF); NOAA, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; USACE, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. This tool helps coastal decision makers choose sites for coastal restoration and resilience projects. The tool identifies areas of open space where projects may have the greatest potential to benefit both human community resilience and fish and wildlife. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – Coastal, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Vector-Borne Disease, Water Quality. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
